physical_skill: Capture a free hold-down ring before unloading its spring-loaded trigger, remove it past the lever end while controlling a hose-suspended valve, then release it off and let it settle. Demonstrated through ordinary contacts with no ring slider, attached grip or programmed latch.
valid_shortcuts: Any successful one-arm manipulation is accepted; squeezing alone is tested but not forbidden.
Ring may be lifted, tilted or displaced by any valid contact route; neither exact trajectory nor squeezing order is scored.
The valve may be supported by ordinary sink surfaces during recovery; no artificial ban on staging. Flow must remain contained, and final hanging/release conditions apply.
Operating the wall supply is outside the specified arm workspace; the task concerns the running pre-rinse head, not identifying a remote control.
distinct_from_nearest: Unlike the closest tongs pull-tab task, the retainer is an external free ring that must be caught as trigger loading is removed; it may fall/reengage and can tilt, while the heavier tool hangs from its ordinary hose. The fluid-control objective adds real containment/release constraints. Distinction rests on these contacts and support conditions, not the recovery label, colours or a mandatory two-hand rule.
remaining_review_risks: Reviewers may still view squeeze-and-retainer operation as too similar to the accepted tongs task; this is a reasoned novelty assessment, not an acceptance guarantee.
Occupation profile proves cleaning duties and workforce size, not the percentage using this exact valve model. Manufacturer identifies industrial-kitchen use.
Undimensioned geometry, spring parameters, segmented hose and packaged product mass are disclosed approximations.
